question: What protection does Canada’s Public Servants Disclosure Protection Act give a federal public servant who makes a protected disclosure?
generated_answer:
The Public Servants Disclosure Protection Act (the Act) provides a public servant who makes a protected disclosure with a range of protections, including:

Protection from reprisal

Protection from reprisal is the most important protection provided by the Act. You are protected from reprisal if you are a public servant, make a protected disclosure and can demonstrate that the reprisal was taken against you because of the disclosure. Reprisal is defined in the Act as any of the following taken by the public servant’s employer because the public servant made a protected disclosure:

a. a disciplinary measure;

b. the demotion of the public servant;

c. the termination of employment of the public servant;

d. any measure that adversely affects the employment or working conditions of the public servant; or

e. a threat to take any of the measures listed above. If you believe that you have been subject to a reprisal, you may file a complaint with the Public Sector Integrity Commissioner (the Commissioner). The Commissioner will then investigate the complaint. If the Commissioner finds that a reprisal was taken, he or she will make recommendations to the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat (the Secretariat) and the public servant’s employer. The Secretariat and the employer must implement the recommendations. If the Commissioner finds that a reprisal was not taken, he or she will inform you of the decision.
